name: Keyboard Lock
plain: Captures keys like Escape and Alt+Tab while in fullscreen.
meaning: Lets games and remote desktops receive keys the browser normally keeps, so a site can trap Escape or Ctrl+W. Works only in fullscreen; a long-press of Escape always exits.

access.prompt_ui: No prompt; works only while the page is in fullscreen.
steps: Locked keys sent to the page

limits.headline: Can capture keys like Escape and Alt+Tab while the page is full screen
limits.user_action: You tap a full screen button in a game or remote desktop
can: Take over keys the browser normally keeps, such as Escape or Alt+Tab
Pass those keys to a game or remote desktop session
Do this only while the page is in full screen
cannot: Trap you for good; holding Escape for about 2 seconds always lets you out
Capture keys when the page is not full screen
Capture the operating system's own protected shortcuts like Ctrl+Alt+Delete
limits.differs: Chrome and Edge support it on desktop. Firefox and Safari do not.

story.what_it_is: Lets a page grab keys like Escape and Alt+Tab when full screen.

marketing.name: Keyboard Lock
marketing.pitch: Describes a way for web apps in full screen to capture keys the browser normally keeps, helpful for games and remote desktops.

story.for_you: You go full screen in a game or remote desktop and keys like Escape go to the game instead of closing it. A message usually says 'Hold Escape to exit full screen'. You feel the page has taken over your keyboard.
story.for_makers: Cloud games and remote work tools need every key to reach the remote computer. Without it, a press of Escape or Alt+Tab would break the stream. Makers also like how it keeps players inside the app.

use_cases.example: A cloud gaming stream sends Escape, Alt and Windows keys to the remote PC, so an in game menu opens instead of exiting full screen.
A remote desktop in the browser forwards Alt+Tab and Ctrl+W to the remote Windows machine.
A browser strategy or shooter game uses Escape for its pause menu while full screen.
An online exam tool locks a student in full screen so keys cannot switch tabs.
A web video editing or 3D tool receives all shortcuts while in full screen.
A bad page could try to trap you in full screen, which is why the browser shows a hold to exit message.

risks: Can trap you in full screen

technical_bounds: Cannot capture Ctrl+Alt+Del or OS shortcuts

abuse: Trapping people in a fullscreen scam page
